To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the learned representations of a deep convolutional neural network trained on a classification problem are highly structured, and that the learned representations can be further structured by imposing a regularization constraint on the training objective function.

The learned representations of a neural network are highly structured, and this structure can be used to improve performance in a wide variety of tasks, such as classification, clustering, retrieval, and transfer learning.

(1) the representations learned by deep convolutional neural network models have a hierarchical structure; (2) the learned representations are highly discriminative; (3) the learned representations contain a large number of spurious features; (4) imposing sparsity on the learned representations can improve their quality; (5) the learned representations can be compressed without loss in performance.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following questions: What is the structure of the learned representations? Can this structure be imposed during the learning process? How does this impact the performance of the network? How can we measure and evaluate the structure of the representations?
understanding the structure of learned representations and the effect that this has on the performance of the network.
the study of the structure of the learned representations and the investigation of the effects of imposing structure during the learning process.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the representations learned by neural networks are highly non-linear and have a very complex structure, and that it is possible to impose structure on the representations by training the network with a regularizer that enforces the learned representations to be smooth.

the structure of these learned representations are highly non-trivial, they are very useful and can be used to solve other tasks, and that it is possible to impose some structure on them during the learning process.
we show that it is indeed possible to impose structure on the learned representations and that this structure has interesting properties.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the learned representations have a structure that is very similar to that of the input images and that this structure is not imposed during the training process but is rather a consequence of the training process itself.
the representations learnt by deep convolutional neural network are not random, but rather have a very interesting structure.
